releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.1
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.1 updates the bundled AnyPS5 core from v0.1.2 to **[v0.1.4](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/releases/tag/v0.1.4)**.

## Changes
- **AnyPS5 core v0.1.4**: the bundled relinker and system libraries now come from the latest upstream release. Existing installs switch to it automatically the next time Studio starts, and each game receives the new libraries on its next launch.
- **Relink hint**: Studio now remembers which core relinked each game. If a game was relinked with an earlier core, the launch log says so and suggests relinking it in Relinker Studio if it fails to start.
- **Verified core downloads**: the bundled core is checked against the SHA-256 checksums AnyPS5 publishes for the release; a mismatch stops the build.
- The NID inspector's "Python 3 not found" message now points to the correct re-audit button.

## After updating
If a game that worked before no longer starts, open **Relinker Studio** and relink it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ramsforge/AnyPS5-Studio/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1

releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.0
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.0 is the biggest update so far: full controller support, playtime tracking, safer handling of your game folders, a faster app that works offline, and a round of security hardening.

## Highlights

### Full controller navigation
- Use the D-pad / left stick to move around every screen (menus, Settings, dialogs, setup and the launcher). Cross selects, Circle goes back, L1 / R1 switch tabs.
- On the game row, Left / Right still pick a game and Cross plays it; press Down to reach the game's buttons.
- Studio ignores the controller while you are playing a game, so button presses never reach Studio behind it.
- Controller rumble now follows the Haptic Feedback setting.
- Arrow keys and Escape work the same way on the keyboard.

### Playtime tracking
- Total playtime and your last session are recorded for every game and shown on the home screen.

### Safer game folders
- Studio only reorganizes folders that actually contain a PS5 title, and no longer moves game assets just because their name looks like a backup (for example `*.baked`).

releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.6

- Integrated Xenia Edge upstream through November 20, 2026. This brings updates across CPU and system emulation, graphics, audio and game content handling while preserving X360 Mobile's Android features and existing fixes.
- Improved handling of game updates and Android storage access. Updated the in-game interface and input handling.
- Continued work on reducing shader-related pauses at the beginning of **Fable II**. New scenes can still pause while shaders are prepared.

Focused checks on Odin 2 covered gameplay in **GTA IV**, **Forza Horizon 2** and **Fable II**, as well as pause, resume and shutdown in **Assassin's Creed**. Results can vary across titles, devices and drivers.

TV mode, synced player profiles and picture-in-picture remain experimental. You can install this release over your current version.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8

This update improves graphics accuracy and adds better diagnostic information for investigating driver performance reports.

## General graphics correction

- Corrected a graphics accuracy issue observed as temporary black, blue or multicoloured corruption during the opening of **Fable II**.
- The correction applies automatically and may also help other games affected by similar rendering problems. No additional game setting is required for this correction; existing recommended settings remain available.
- Verified through two opening runs reaching the first childhood gameplay scene on Odin 2. Later scenes, full campaigns and other GPUs still need testing.
- This is an accuracy improvement, with no general FPS increase promised. Brief pauses may still occur when new shaders are prepared.

## Driver diagnostics and session sharing

- Added more useful texture and performance information for investigating reported slowdowns with **RADV on Exynos/Xclipse**.
- Gameplay measurement recordings are now associated with their session and can be included when using **Share session bundle** from Session history.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7

This update brings a general graphics correctness improvement and experimental picture-in-picture support for external media apps.

## Graphics correction

- Fixed the horizontally divided image and missing lower portion observed in the opening real-time cutscene of **Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning**.
- This is a general core correction, applied automatically without additional settings. It may benefit other games affected by similar rendering problems, but wider game and GPU coverage still needs testing.
- Verified through repeated starts and progression to character creation on Odin 2. This does not certify the full campaign or promise a general FPS increase.

## Experimental picture-in-picture

- Keep the game full screen while a compatible external media app uses Android's floating video window.
- Added an app selector with PiP compatibility indicators, an optional media link, and controls in the game menu. Find these options under **Settings → App → Appearance and startup**.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6

Maintenance update focused on optional driver compatibility and updated game recommendations.

- Added an optional experimental texture compatibility setting for RADV on Samsung Xclipse. It is disabled by default and has not yet been verified on Xclipse hardware. Successful driver loading, rendering and performance are not guaranteed; memory use may increase.
- Added recommended settings for **Mobile Suit Gundam: Operation Troy**, restoring the visible world in the first map tested on Odin 2. A complete game copy is required; other devices and the full campaign remain unverified.
- Added recommendations for **Sonic Free Riders with the adapted No Kinect mod**. The compatible adapted mod and its designated launcher are required: settings alone do not repair the original mod, and the mod is not bundled with the app. Menus and two tutorial stages were tested; uneven steering remains under investigation, and full-game compatibility is not confirmed.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5

Maintenance update focused on game loading reliability and clearer driver diagnostics.

- Improved handling of extracted games, disc images and installed game containers.
- Added a per-game startup executable selector for games with multiple launchers.
- Improved reliability when loading additional game modules and title updates, with safer recovery after failed launches.
- Improved recognition of game files and preservation of launch preferences across library updates and shortcuts.
- More precise on-device Vulkan driver diagnostics, including the image check that failed and available error information.

Custom drivers remain device-dependent. More detailed diagnostics help investigate compatibility; they do not guarantee successful RADV loading or fix every game or mod.

Install over your current version; no uninstall is required. Keep a backup of your profiles and saves as usual.

releases.name: Cemu Plus 0.4.1
releases.body:
Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

## What's new

### Game updates
- **Use update** in the settings of a game, under Update, turns its installed update off, and the game runs as its base version. It's only shown for games with an update, and applies the next time the game starts. The game card shows the version the game runs as
- Games whose update doesn't work in Cemu have it off by default, with a note under the switch saying it's recommended off. **Why?** opens the reason

### Fixes
- ZombiU no longer stays on a black screen after the Ubisoft logo. Its update (v32) doesn't work in Cemu, so it's off by default and ZombiU runs as its base version


## Frame generation setup
1. Copy `Lossless.dll` from your own copy of Lossless Scaling (its installation folder on Windows) to your device.
2. In Cemu Plus open **Settings → Graphics settings → Frame generation (Lossless Scaling)** and tap **Select Lossless.dll**.
3. Enable frame generation there or from the in-game menu, where the multiplier, target frame rate and motion estimation resolution can be changed while playing.

## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.15: más rendimiento

### Cambios

- **Más rendimiento en procesadores con 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88/G99, MT6769/MT6789 y similares). En la versión anterior dejamos de fijar los hilos del juego a los núcleos rápidos en estos procesadores, y en algunos volvió el lag. Ahora el hilo principal del juego, el que más trabaja, va en los núcleos rápidos, y los demás hilos los reparte Android. Con 4 o más núcleos rápidos no cambia nada: todos los hilos van en ellos.

Ahora se anota una sola vez. Otras líneas repetitivas (texturas convertidas en la CPU, entrada de teclado, liberación de superficies) también se limitan. Además de ahorrar CPU, el registro de los reportes conserva lo importante.

Dos APK: **arm64** y **armeabi-v7a**. Android 10+, Vulkan 1.1+. Misma firma; se instalan como actualización. Se adjunta `NFSU1-v0.2.15-SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Underground 1 Android Evolved v0.2.12: volver al juego sin cierres y reportes completos

### Correcciones

- **Cierre al volver al juego.** Si salías a otra app y volvías, el juego podía cerrarse en el primer fotograma. Android libera la ventana del juego al pasar a segundo plano, pero la superficie Vulkan seguía usándola y se destruía después. Ahora la superficie conserva su ventana hasta que se destruye.

### Reportes más útiles

- **El resumen del issue ya trae las líneas del juego.** Antes se tomaban de logcat y, cuando pulsabas *Reportar*, Android ya las había borrado: casi todos los issues llegaban con "últimas líneas del juego" vacío. Ahora salen del registro propio del juego (`game.log`), y logcat solo aporta las líneas del cierre.
- **Lecturas de archivo incompletas en el registro.** Si el juego pide más datos de los que recibe de un archivo, se anota el archivo, la posición y su tamaño. Así podremos ver si un cierre viene de un archivo del juego dañado o incompleto.

This release finalizes the 5.0 series.

Emulation accuracy

releases.name: Xenoblade 3 port v0.4.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

# reNut Android 0.4.0

An experimental Android port of **Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts** (Xbox 360), built from a static recompilation of the game.

> **Heads up:** this is a vibe-coded port. Expect bugs, rough edges and uneven compatibility across devices.

## Features

- **Local multiplayer** for two players: connect a second gamepad and it joins as player 2.
- **No GPU command-stream emulation.** The game's Direct3D calls are translated straight into Vulkan through Plume, the same renderer layer UnleashedRecomp uses, with shaders recompiled ahead of time. Some Xbox 360 GPU behaviour (resolves, texture formats, tessellation, memexport) is still emulated on the host.
- **In-app achievements** section.
- **Graphics options** to trade quality for performance:
  - internal resolution
  - texture resolution
  - shadow resolution
- **Adrenotools driver support**, a bundled Turnip driver and Turnip tuning options.
- **Save import and export.**

## Performance

On a Galaxy S23 Ultra the game runs above 30 FPS at the original graphics settings. Other devices have not been tested, so your results will vary. If it runs slowly, lower the internal, texture and shadow resolution.

releases.body:
### Fixed

- The Linux release plays game movies: it links a small static FFmpeg (FFmpeg's own H.264, HEVC, VP8/VP9, AAC, Opus, Vorbis and MP3 decoders, no other libraries), so it needs no FFmpeg on the system and works whatever FFmpeg version the distribution has. releases.name: v0.1.8-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The emulated display is 1080p by default (it was 2160p), in the launcher, `rps5e-cli run` and the test scripts: games that size their output to the display render a quarter of the pixels and the window scales the picture, which is much lighter on the GPU. 2160p (and 720p) stay selectable in the launcher's settings, per game, and with `--display-resolution` / `RPS5E_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION`. Games that do not ask for the display's resolution are shown a 2160p display as on the console.
- System functions answer as measured on a PS5 in a game process: a trylock of an adaptive mutex by its owner returns EINVAL (was EBUSY); `sceKernelAddAmprEvent` on a deleted or null event queue returns EBADF (was success); `sceSystemServiceReceiveEvent` with no event pending returns "no event" for any pointer and leaves the buffer untouched (it wrote an empty event first, and a null pointer was a parameter error); the `sceNetGetSockInfo` record carries the socket priority 0x10.
- `sceVideoOutSetFlipRate` checks the handle before the rate and accepts rate 3 (a flip every fourth vblank), as on a PS5.

releases.name: 0.1.7-alpha - 2026-11-13
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Ghost of Yōtei no longer freezes after its shaders are compiled (#3). Two causes:
  - Planning the resources of a shader walked the shader's whole value graph again for every word of every buffer descriptor; on this game's largest shaders that took minutes on the GPU command thread, with nothing submitted meanwhile. Each value is now walked once per shader.
  - A few compute shaders became SPIR-V modules of 2.7-3.2 million words that the GPU driver compiled for 15 minutes and more while the game waited (the driver keeps the result, so only the first run on a machine stalled). The largest is now 0.6 million words and builds in about 40 s on an RTX 5090, once; the results are the same, bit for bit (device tests over every buffer format, page-crossing elements and partial EXEC):

releases.name: 0.1.6-alpha - 2026-11-12
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Windows: controllers work out of the box. The release archive now carries `SDL3.dll`: the emulator loads SDL at run time and Windows has none of its own, so no controller was found ("SDL3 not available") unless the file was added by hand. The message for a missing library now says where to put it ([#4](https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/issues/4)).


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/compare/v0.1.5-alpha...v0.1.6-alpha

releases.name: 1.0.5-alpha
releases.body:
### Changed

- The automatic choice of the recording thread (`RPS5E_GPU_RECORD_THREAD=auto`) no longer turns it off while the command interpreter also has to wait for room in its queue (`RPS5E_POLICY_FULL`). SILENT HILL: The Short Message's heavy room about 10 fps instead of 8; GTA V with `RPS5E_BDA=1` 47 fps instead of 42.
- `RPS5E_BDA=1` (experimental direct guest memory reads) no longer changes the default of `RPS5E_LABELS_AT_EOP`: with its old default (`1`) GTA V never left its start menu. GTA V's city in Performance mode with `RPS5E_BDA=1`: 47-48 fps against 37 without it; still off by default.
- The emulator's own small writes into GPU-watched guest memory (memcpy/memset inside one page, packets of the command-buffer builders) mark the page written before the store instead of taking a page fault (`RPS5E_PREMARK_SMALL`). GTA V's city in Performance mode: write faults per frame ~1550 → ~320; over the same stretch of the scene the frame rate rises by about 2.5 % (36.6 → 37.4 fps).

## What's New
#### Added
- Added **MIDI** support, allowing some games to play MIDI audio. The software comes with an open-source soundfont by [default](https://musical-artifacts.com/artifacts/1517), and you can also install your preferred soundfont in the `Settings` (currently, only SF2 format is supported). Download Windows MIDI Soundfont [here](https://musical-artifacts.com/artifacts/713).
- Improved **OpenXR** suooport. Many thanks to **Luboš V.** , his work making OpenXR support possible and better.
- Improved Game Controller Support, you can now selectively use **XInput** or **DInput** mapping. Linear triggers now work with both mapping modes. For trigger button, if it’s not working correctly, try adjusting the trigger button mode in the `Settings` to match your controller.
- Added the feature to automatically set the container's **Locale**. You can now also adjust `LC_ALL` settings in the container editing interface.
- Added Landscape And **Portrait Mode** switching features. You can now switch to portrait mode using the container's resolution settings or `Toggle Orientation` button of the left-side navigation bar.

releases.name: Winlator 7.1.2 with Native Glibc
releases.body:
#### Added
- Added support for `Box64rc`, allowing different Box64 parameters to be set for each process.
- Added `virtual touchscreen` support, also referred to as `direct cursor` support. True touchscreen support requires implementing the XInput2 extension.
- Added support for Chinese. And any corrections to the translation are welcome.
- Added an `content manager`, allowing you to install Wine, graphics drivers, or DX wrappers externally.
- Added the ability to reinstall system files, allowing recovery even if the system files are accidentally damaged.
- Added more VKD3D feature level options.
- Added android `file provider` feature, allowing access to the Winlator data directory through the file manager.
- Added the ability to add `shortcuts` to the home screen, allowing you to launch your programs directly from the desktop. Shortcut changes will be synced in real-time.

#### Fixed
- Fixed the crash issue that occurred when running programs with long Japanese or Chinese titles.
- Corrected the button styling in the DXVK configuration dialog.
- Fixed certain abnormal issues on some SoCs (such as 870), by compiling Box64 with the `BAD_SIGNAL` parameter enabled.

releases.name: Winlator 7.1.1 with Native Glibc
releases.body:
#### Added
- Added `dxvk-2.4` and `dxvk-gplasync-2.4`, and set dxvk-2.3.1 as the default dxvk.

- Added `vkd3d-2.13`.
- Added an older version of `box64` (`box64-2.8`).

#### Changed

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/longjunyu2/winlator/compare/v7.1.0...v7.1.1

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.0 (beta 46): amiibo
releases.body:
**Beta 46.** Agora dá para usar amiibo no jogo, sem figura física, e os menus ficaram mais fáceis de usar com o dedo.

## amiibo (#181)

Um leitor de amiibo virtual, com as 36 figuras que o jogo reconhece: as da série Zelda, o Lobo Link, e as de outras séries que dão itens.

- **Como usar:** escolha a runa amiibo e aponte para onde os itens vão cair. Depois toque **de novo no botão da runa** (no layout clássico, o L): o menu abre já na escolha do amiibo, em Controles. Escolha a figura e toque em **Encostar o amiibo**. O menu fecha e o jogo lê a figura.
- Com um controle, ou fora da runa: abra o menu e vá em Controles > amiibo.
- Cada figura dá seus itens uma vez por dia, como no Switch. Os dados de cada figura ficam salvos no app: o coração e o progresso do Lobo Link continuam entre as partidas.

## Menus no toque

- **As listas rolam com o dedo**, com inércia, inclusive as que abrem (como a de amiibo): antes era preciso arrastar uma barra de rolagem fina. As barras e os puxadores também ficaram maiores.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.13 (beta 45): correção para o travamento da Mali nas lutas
releases.body:
**Beta 45.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos de luta na Mali, e três mudanças de desempenho para a Mali.

## O travamento da Mali (#401)

Na Mali-G1 Ultra do #401, o jogo travava depois de alguns minutos de luta (com muitos efeitos), no modo Nativo e no Recompilado. Os logs mostravam uma thread do jogo presa percorrendo a lista de blocos livres do alocador de memória do jogo, que dava a volta.

- **A causa provável:** na Mali, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo é copiado de volta quando a GPU termina. Fora da "arena" de memória global, essa cópia era da faixa inteira, e desfazia o que o jogo tinha escrito ali no meio-tempo, inclusive os cabeçalhos e os links da lista de blocos livres, que ficam logo antes dos buffers. A 0.4.10 já fazia a cópia certa, mas só dentro da arena, que nunca liga nas Malis cujo driver oferece a importação de memória (como a G1 Ultra).
- **O que muda:** agora volta só o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e o que o jogo escreveu no meio-tempo fica. Quando isso acontece, o log diz `copy-back: a word the game wrote meanwhile kept`.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.12 (beta 44): eixos do giroscópio do controle e FIFO no Adreno 7xx
releases.body:
**Beta 44.** Duas opções novas, uma correção do HUD nos santuários e duas mudanças para a Mali.

## Novidades

- **Eixos do giroscópio do controle** (Configurações > Controles; #511, #521): para controles cujo giroscópio informa os eixos em outra ordem, como o DataFrog B01 e o Flydigi Direwolf 4, e a mira anda de lado quando você levanta o controle. As opções são "Como o controle informa", "Trocar esquerda-direita e cima-baixo", "Trocar cima-baixo e inclinação" e "Trocar esquerda-direita e inclinação". A troca vale na hora.
- **Esperar a tela (FIFO)** (tela inicial, em Compatibilidade do driver; #367): num Adreno 730, a imagem congelava por segundos enquanto o som e o jogo continuavam. Esperar a tela resolveu. A opção tem Automático, Ligado e Desligado. O Automático liga no Adreno 7xx e deixa desligado nas outras GPUs, como antes. Se a imagem congelar assim no seu aparelho, ligue.

## Correções

- **Minimapa em cima, nos santuários** (#261): com o minimapa em cima, as barras de som e temperatura subiam e desciam a cada segundo dentro dos santuários. Uma peça do HUD que aparece e some ali era tomada pelo disco do minimapa. Agora só o disco conta.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.11 (beta 43): o jogo não fecha mais por falta de memória no Adreno 640
releases.body:
**Beta 43.** Uma correção para o jogo que fechava depois de alguns minutos num Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM.

## Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM (#520)

O log do OnePlus 7 Pro (Adreno 640, 8 GB) mostrou que a GPU ficava sem memória: depois de 8 a 28 minutos, o driver não conseguia mais criar os pipelines (os "programas" que desenham cada tipo de objeto), e o jogo fechava logo depois.

- **A causa:** no Turnip, a opção **Memória do jogo na GPU (Turnip)** no Automático coloca os ~3,1 GB da memória do jogo direto na GPU. Num aparelho com 8 GB, isso deixava pouca memória para o próprio driver.
- **O que muda:** num Adreno 6xx com 8 GB de RAM ou menos, o Automático agora deixa essa opção desligada, e o jogo trabalha com cópias. A tela inicial avisa isso embaixo da opção. Com cópias, o mesmo aparelho jogou 2 horas sem fechar, com o texto certo e de 13 a 16 fps (antes, de 10 a 14). Quem quiser pode ligar a opção na mão.
- **E se a memória acabar mesmo assim:** antes, um pipeline que falhava por falta de memória ficava perdido até o fim da sessão, e o que ele desenhava sumia. Agora os pipelines sem uso são liberados na hora, e o que falhou é criado de novo 5 s depois.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.10 (beta 42): uma correção para o travamento na Mali
releases.body:
**Beta 42.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos nas GPUs que trabalham no modo cópia (Mali e o driver de fábrica da Qualcomm).

## O travamento depois de alguns minutos (#401, #489)

Os logs da 0.4.9 mostraram que o problema não era a ordem das threads nos núcleos: com a opção nova ligada, o jogo travou do mesmo jeito, e o laço estava no **alocador de memória do jogo**, que percorria uma lista de blocos livres danificada.

- **A causa provável:** nessas GPUs, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo volta para ela depois que a GPU termina. Cada pedaço era conferido ("a GPU mudou, o jogo não") e depois copiado inteiro. Se uma thread do jogo escrevesse no mesmo pedaço entre as duas coisas, por exemplo nos dados que o alocador guarda ao lado de cada bloco, essa escrita se perdia. Uma escrita perdida ali deixa a lista de blocos livres em laço, e o jogo para.
- **A correção:** só volta o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e cada palavra só é escrita se o jogo não a mudou nesse meio-tempo. A escrita do jogo nunca se perde.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.1
releases.body:
# Changes (**Mainly bugfixes!**)
- Linux: Accepting a Netplay invite through Discord without having melonRA open would show an "Unknown protocol" error message, this was because it wasn't registered properly with the rest of apps in the OS, it now handles it properly.
- Netplay: Errors whilst syncing up instances and saves with the "hidden consoles" used for Netplay.
- Netplay: Closing the room closes the open UDP port after a while.
- Netplay: Closing a room with nobody connected is now instant.
- _Other minor Netplay fixes._
- Rewind kept its history after inserting a cartridge or booting up firmware. Meaning that, rewinding could make you rewind to a previous game. This has been patched.
- _Other general fixes._
- Casual mode offline unlocks were dropped if the saved login expired when its sent, now it is kept for the next login. And now the text is clearer when you play offline.

releases.name: XRecomp v0.19.0
releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.19.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A second Xbox 360 performance night, measured headless on Warhammer: Battle March. Frames and save states are byte
identical to 0.18.0, except where a change is opt-in or per title (below).

- **Guest CPU**: `MmQueryStatistics` keeps a page count instead of scanning (it was half of the boot's host CPU). The
  VMX helpers work on 16- and 8-bit lanes, use the compiler's vector extensions and are inlined. Host CPU: the boot
  is 3× faster and in-game play 1.8× (141 → 79 ms of guest time per swap). The scheduler turn is cheaper and makes
  the same decisions. Prepare is not slower: the VMX-heavy files compile 27–41 % faster with NDK clang.
- **Renderer**: 16-bit resolve formats take the fast path, and the stencil is read back in 2 passes instead of 8.
  Tiled addressing is worked out per tile row, texture rows are read 16 bytes at a time, texture memory is hashed in
  8 lanes and packed vertex formats use tables. Renderer CPU per swap is about half of 0.18.0's.

releases.name: XRecomp v0.18.0
releases.body:
# XRecomp 0.18.0

<!-- Highlights: what changed, what works, known problems. Written by hand, kept across updates. -->

A speed night on every console but the Xbox 360. Every change is bit-exact: frame, RAM and audio hashes over 600
frames or more are identical to 0.17.0, and lockstep with the interpreters holds.

| Console | x86-64 instructions per frame (bench) | Prepare again? |
|---|---|---|
| GBA | 9.06M → 7.09M (−22 %) | yes |
| PS1 | 8.08M → 6.49M (−20 %) | no |
| N64 | 6.58M → 5.65M (−14 %) | yes |
| GameCube | audio mix −24 %, GX front end −14 % | no |
| Xbox | float stack code −30 % on arm64 (`fistp` without libm) | yes |

- **GBA**: the prefetch model charges a run of plain instructions in one call, and exact segment cycles keep lifted
  code running (instructions handed to the interpreter −43 %).
- **PS1**: the SPU skips idle voices and silent reverb; handed instructions run in one loop; the HLE interrupt entry
  and exit copy registers in blocks.
- **N64**: COUNT reads stay in lifted code (polling screens 7× cheaper); one range test per store; the AI resampler
  skips silence; a cheaper dispatcher hit.

Thirteenth beta of KINGDOM HEARTS 358/2 Days for Android on **[khdays-port 0.1.5](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-port/releases/tag/v0.1.5)**, Yokimitsuro's native PC port that this Android version follows. All the credit for the port itself goes there.

## What's new since beta 12

- **Sharper tutorial pages and lower-screen menus on one screen.** When the lower screen is shown big over the whole picture (a tutorial page, the load menu, the world list, a mission's page), it is now drawn at the size it is shown at, and a tutorial page's text is drawn sharp on its own. Before, it was drawn at the lower screen's own resolution and stretched, so the text came out soft.
- **Far-away enemies move every frame.** From khdays-port's development branch: Days only updated enemies far from the camera every other frame, which made them stutter on a smooth picture.

Coming from an earlier beta? The game offers this update itself on the title screen, or install the APK below by hand; your game, HD files and saves are kept.

## What's new since beta 11

A beta about speed with the HD pack's KH2 models.

- **Scenes with the KH2 character models are no longer slow.** A KH2 model with a coat made the whole 3D picture take a slow path. On a Mali-G57 tablet the scene after Day 7 ran at 16-22 pictures a second; now 51-60. Stronger devices gain too in close-ups.
- **Enhanced character shadows cost much less.** With the setting on, an AYN Thor went from 93 to 62 pictures a second in the Grey Area; now 86.
- **A frozen picture on Mali devices is recovered from.** When the graphics driver stopped answering, the picture stood still for good while the game went on. The game now notices and carries on after a short hitch, and one of the two moments where it happened is gone.

- **Much faster starts on some devices.** The graphics card's programs are now kept between starts instead of being made again every time. On the AYN Odin (Adreno 630) the screen stayed black for one to four minutes at every start; now it is about 3 seconds. Other devices start a little faster too.
- **"Compiling shaders – First boot only"** shows on the first start after installing or updating, while those programs are made, instead of a black screen. That first start can still take a minute or so on older devices.

releases.name: v2.2.0
releases.body:
## New since v2.1.6 (last stable)

- **Steam ISO manual export** — Steam ISO files (`<Game Name>.iso` to `Downloads/front end/`) are no longer written automatically on every game list load. They are now written on demand via the **FileDownload** (↓) button in the My Games top bar, preventing unnecessary writes and duplicate file churn.
- **ISO duplicate skip** — ISO export now checks if the file already exists in `Downloads/front end/` before writing; skips silently if it does, preventing duplicate entries.
- **Game name sanitization** — Game names are sanitized before being used in MediaStore queries and ISO file creation (colons and other illegal filename characters are replaced), fixing a crash/failure when Steam game names contain colons or other special characters.

---

## Full Feature Set

**Core**
- No root required — uses Android's Storage Access Framework (SAF) for secure folder access.
- Single data/ grant — one SAF permission at `<package>/data` covers components, virtual containers, and shadercache simultaneously.
- Multi-app support — automatically detects all installed GameHub variants side by side.

releases.name: v2.1.9-pre
releases.body:
Move Steam ISO export from automatic (every load) to a manual button.

The download arrow (⬇) button appears in the My Games top bar when an app is selected and Steam games are loaded. Tapping it writes/updates the ISOs for all Steam games on demand.

Navigation is now instant — no more SteamRepository.fetch() + MediaStore operations firing silently on every tab visit.

releases.name: v2.1.8-pre
releases.body:
Fix Counter-Strike: Source (and any game with : in the name) creating a new ISO every launch.

**Root cause:** Steam game names with colons (e.g. `Counter-Strike: Source`) get stored in MediaStore with the colon replaced by `_`. The existence check queried with the original name (colon), found nothing, and inserted again — MediaStore then auto-renamed the new file to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Sanitize filename chars `[/\\:*?"<>|]` → `_` before any MediaStore query or insert, so both sides always agree on the name.

releases.name: v2.1.7-pre
releases.body:
Fix duplicate ISO files in Downloads/front end/ on every app launch.

**Root cause:** The old code called MediaStore delete() then insert() each launch. On Android, delete() removes the catalog entry but not the physical file — so insert() would see the file already on disk and auto-rename it to `Counter-Strike_ Source (1).iso`, `(2).iso`, etc.

**Fix:** Query first. If the ISO already exists, skip writing it entirely. No duplicates.

The headline: the slabs over Gerudo Town are gone, and motion at the frame rate limit is steadier, with and without frame generation.

- **Gerudo Town slabs fixed.** After a visit to the Depths, huge slabs of terrain could hang over Gerudo Town. The ground there is built from a map the game draws in parts; the undrawn parts now hold what the game expects instead of leftovers from other images.

- **TAA anti-aliasing (docked).** A new Anti-aliasing choice that blends several frames into each picture. Edges shimmer far less while you pan, and the picture looks a little softer. TAA softness sets how soft.
- **Picture softness (docked).** Sets how the game enlarges its picture to the screen: Original (the game's own sharp filter), Neutral, Soft or Softer. The softer choices calm edges that crawl as the camera moves.

releases.body:
Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-17. Three new settings, an audio output picker in the game's pause menu, and Android's Performance Game Mode.

## What's new

- Three settings for each game. Under Input, Menu button shows or hides the on-screen menu button (Back still opens the menu), and Controllers either gives each controller its own player or makes them all player 1. Under Performance, GPU turbo holds the GPU at its highest clock, always or only while frames run late.
- The pause menu's Game tab has an Audio output row. It sends the game's sound to the output you pick, such as the device speaker or Bluetooth headphones, until the game ends.
- Pagurin declares Android's Performance Game Mode. With Pagurin set to Performance, a game keeps its own frame rate instead of stepping down to 40 or 30.
- A game added with the import tool while Pagurin is open now shows its new settings and size right away. In 0.2.1 you had to reopen Pagurin.
- The group headings in a game's settings (Graphics, Input, Performance and so on) are in the app's accent colour, so the groups stand apart.
- The README is reorganised, with a Quick start first.

## Before you update

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.1
releases.body:
Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-11: games can use local play over Wi-Fi, and a controller's face buttons can follow their labels.

## What's new

- **Local play over Wi-Fi.** Pagurin now has the network permissions a port's host asks for, so a game whose profile turns on local play (`DM_LAN`, such as Animal Crossing: New Horizons) can reach other players on the same Wi-Fi.
- **Face buttons setting.** A game's Input settings have a **Face buttons** row: **Position** (the Switch's layout, the default) or **Label** (A is the button marked A, as on an Xbox-style controller). It's the same setting as the pause menu's Face buttons row.
- **The import tool cleans up `sysdata/` too.** A port made with `--firmware` carries system data, and running the tool again now removes what an older port left there.

## Before you update

- The Face buttons row only shows for a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-09 or later. An older port doesn't read the setting, so the row stays hidden.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.0
releases.body:
GPU drivers now work the way nx2android's main branch takes them, and a game can be removed from the library.

## What's new

- **GPU drivers for nx2android's main branch.** Each game picks one of three:
  - **The game's own driver** (the default): the one its port was made with (`porter port --vulkan-driver`), or the system's if the port has none.
  - **The system driver**, even for a port that brought its own.
  - **A driver you added from a file.** Pagurin carries libadrenotools itself, so this also works for ports made without a driver.
- **Remove a game** from its settings tab. You choose whether to keep its save; a kept save is picked up again if you add the game back.
- **The import tool cleans up.** Running it again removes files an older port of the game left behind in `host/`, `mods/`, `RomFS/` and `aoc/`.
- The game page shows its button hints in the same order on every tab. LB and RB are on the tab bar.

## Before you update

- Choosing a driver needs a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-03 or later. An older port still runs, on the system's driver. Port it again to choose a driver.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release. Pagurin keeps your Android ports of games from other platforms in one app, such as those made with [nx2android](https://github.com/shirai91/nx2android), instead of a separate app per game.

## What's in it

- A library of your ports, with search and sorting.
- Settings for each game: docked or handheld mode, the on-screen gamepad, rumble, the frame rate counter and the engine's performance switches. A game only shows the settings its own host reads.
- One game language for every game. A game that doesn't have it runs in English.
- GPU drivers, added from a file and picked per game.
- Save export, import and delete. Import also takes another app's save folder or a zip.
- Games added from a PC with the import tool, or moved over from ports already installed as their own apps (AYN devices, or Shizuku elsewhere).

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Pagurin-0.1.0.apk` | The app. Android 10 or later, arm64. |
| `pagurin-import.exe` | The import tool for Windows. On other systems, run `tools/pagurin_import.py` with Python 3.9 or later. |

releases.body:
> **Beta.** Playable at the 30 FPS cap on the AYN Thor, with known graphics bugs and only two devices tested so far.

**Bug-fix update to 0.6.0.** Installs over 0.6.0 and keeps your saves (same signing key).

**Bring your own game:** you need an ISO of a supported Fable II disc. This APK contains no game data (no art, audio, maps or video).

## What's new
- **Fixed: purple strip along the bottom of the screen.** Fable II clears some buffers by drawing a rectangle over them. The emulator assumed these covered all of the GPU's render memory, so the last few rows of a half-resolution buffer kept stale data and reached the screen. Clears now only replace the rows they actually draw. No performance cost: still a steady 30 FPS on the Thor.

## Install
1. Download **FableDroid-0.6.1-beta.apk** below and open it on your device.
2. First install only: copy your Fable II ISO to the device, open the app, tap **Select game ISO**, choose the file and wait for it to install.
3. Tap **Play**.

releases.name: FableDroid 0.6 Beta
releases.body:
> **Beta.** Playable at the 30 FPS cap on the AYN Thor, with known graphics bugs and only two devices tested so far.

**Fable II, running natively on Android.** First public build of FableDroid.

**Bring your own game:** you need an ISO of a supported Fable II disc. This APK contains no game data (no art, audio, maps or video).

## Install
1. Download **FableDroid-0.6.0-beta.apk** below and open it on your device.
2. Copy your Fable II ISO to the device.
3. Open the app, tap **Select game ISO**, choose the file and wait for it to install.
4. Tap **Play**.

Requires Android 12+, 64-bit, about 7 GB free (plus the ISO while installing). An Adreno 7xx GPU (Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 or newer) is strongly recommended. On non-Adreno GPUs, choose **GPU drivers / downloads → System driver**.

## Highlights
- Native arm64 + Vulkan, 30 FPS cap held on an AYN Thor (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2) at 720p
- Low-latency mode and high tick rate on by default
- FXAA + dithered foliage instead of slow MSAA
- Install straight from the ISO on the device, one-tap save backup
- Controller remapping, touch controls with a layout editor
- Bundled Mesa Turnip driver plus a driver manager

## Supported versions

hardsilinder-fabledroid.latest_body:
FableDroid 0.9.0: about 99% of the game's code is now decompiled to native code (59,958 of 60,481 functions: game code 99.5%, library code 98.5%). The remaining ~520 functions still run through the recompiled path and are being rewritten by hand.

### Status
- Tested on the AYN Thor (Adreno 740): boots, loads a save and plays the full forest route with no crashes.
- Performance on the Thor: the default is a locked 30 FPS (the Xbox 360's cap, steadiest). With the experimental 60 FPS setting (Settings > Frame rate) it runs about 57 FPS median, with lows around 37 FPS in heavy scenes; 40 and 60 FPS can stutter briefly while walking.
- Adreno 8xx (Odin 3, Snapdragon 8 Elite/Gen 5) and Mali are still untested on this build. Reports and logs are very welcome.

### Known issues
- The item wheel in the on-screen display occasionally draws incorrectly.

### Installing
Installs over 0.6.x as a normal update; your game files and saves are kept.

New installs: install the APK and follow the setup steps in the README. You still need your own copy of Fable II (Game of the Year edition); no game files are included.
